title: Sky colours and starlight

lessons.objective: Connect the blue daytime sky to sunlight scattered by air molecules.
Explain how the low Sun’s longer air path changes the colours reaching us.
Distinguish refraction and reflection, and connect a rainbow to the colours already in sunlight.
Explain atmospheric twinkling, compare low and high stars and understand why planets usually look steadier.

outcomes: Explain why a blue sky does not need a nearby sea.
Compare the wavelengths of blue and red light.
Connect a low Sun with a longer route through the air and warmer arriving light.
Follow sunlight bending and reflecting inside a raindrop.
Explain why a rainbow’s appearance depends on the observer’s position.
Connect moving air to twinkling stars, and explain why planets usually look steadier.
description: Why is the sky blue, how are rainbows formed and why do stars twinkle? Follow light through air and water in short, connected science lessons.
introduction:
A blue afternoon becomes an orange evening. A shower brings a rainbow, and after dark a star seems to flicker. What is the light doing?

Start with sunlight scattered by air. Then follow light through a raindrop and discover how moving air changes our view of the stars. Read at your own pace; the short quizzes are optional.
prerequisites: No science background needed. Each new term is explained as it appears.
